(p-86)In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Surah ash-Shu'ara' (The Poets)

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they do not become believers.﴾ (26:3).

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in the beginning of Surah "al-Kahf," in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over their traces, if they do not believe in this narration, in sorrow.﴾ [al-Kahf: 6], and at the end of Surah "al-Hijr," in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not grieve over them﴾ [al-Hijr: 88], and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We certainly know that your breast is constricted by what they say﴾ [al-Hijr: 97].

"Allah's saying (the Exalted): ﴿Have they not looked at the earth, how many noble pairs of every kind We have caused to grow therein?﴾ (7) ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign, but most of them are not believers.﴾ (8)

In this noble verse, He (majestic and exalted) points out that the abundance of what He causes to grow in the earth, of every noble pair—that is, every good kind (sinf) of the varieties of plants—contains a sign indicating His perfect power.

We have explained in several places in this blessed Book that the reviving of the earth after its death, and the growth of plants in it after their non-existence, are among the decisive proofs of the resurrection of people after death.

We have also explained the indication of the Qur'anic verses to this in Surat al-Baqarah, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you…﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and sent down from the sky water, and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 21–22]; and at the beginning of Surat al-Nahl, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿It is He who sent down from the sky water; from it is drink, and from it is [vegetation] upon which you graze. He causes to grow for you thereby the crops, the olives, the palm trees, the grapes, and from all the fruits﴾ [al-Nahl: 10–11], and so on."

Al-Shinqiti's commentary (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 26, verse 10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when your Lord called out to Musa: "Go to the wrongdoing people,"﴾ (10) ﴿the people of Fir'awn. Will they not fear Allah?﴾ (11).

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "Maryam," in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We called him from the right side of the mount and brought him near as a confidant﴾ [Maryam: 52].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 26, verse 12:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He said, "My Lord, I fear that they will deny me.﴾ (12) ﴿And my breast will be constricted, and my tongue will not be eloquent.﴾"

(p-87) His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse concerning His prophet Musa, peace be upon him and upon our Prophet: "Indeed, I fear that they will deny me," meaning: because I killed a soul from among them, and I fled from them when I feared that they would kill me in retaliation for the person I had killed from among them. What clarifies this meaning is the sequence with "fa" (then) in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed I killed a soul from among them, so I fear that they will kill me."﴾ [al-Qasas: 33]; because whoever fears being killed expects to be denied. As for His saying, ﴿and my tongue will not be eloquent﴾, meaning: on account of the impediment mentioned in His saying, may He be exalted, concerning Musa: ﴿And loosen the knot from my tongue﴾ ﴿that they may understand my speech.﴾ [Ta-Ha: 27-28]. We have already discussed this in the commentary on the verse of "Ta-Ha." These are some of the verses that indicate what relates to this topic.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 26, verse 13:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿So send [word] to Harun﴾ (13).

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah Maryam, in the discussion of His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And We gave him, out of Our mercy, his brother Harun as a prophet﴾ [Maryam: 53].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 26, verse 14:

Regarding His prophet Musa, the Exalted said: ﴿And they have a charge against me, so I fear that they will kill me﴾ (14). Here He did not specify this charge that they hold against him, for which he fears they will kill him because of it. But He has specified in another place that the charge mentioned is his killing of their companion (al-Ghabtiyy, the Egyptian man). For the Exalted explicitly stated the killing mentioned in His saying: ﴿He said, "My Lord, I have killed a soul among them, so I fear that they will kill me"﴾ [al-Qasas: 33]. So His saying ﴿I have killed a soul among them﴾ explains His saying ﴿And they have a charge against me﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 14], and for this reason He connected each of the two statements to the other with the particle "fa" (so, therefore). As for His saying ﴿so I fear that they will kill me﴾, the Exalted has clarified the story of Musa's killing of the man in His saying in "al-Qasas": ﴿And he entered the city at a time of unawareness of its people, and found therein two men fighting, one from his own faction and the other from his enemy. So the one from his own faction called for his help against the one from his enemy, and Musa struck him and killed him﴾ [al-Qasas: 15]. His saying "fa-qada 'alayhi" means he killed him, and that is the charge mentioned in this verse of "ash-Shu'ara'".

The Exalted has also made clear that He forgave His prophet Musa that charge mentioned, in His saying: ﴿He said, "My Lord, I have wronged myself, so forgive me." So He forgave him﴾ (the verse) [al-Qasas: 16].

The Qur'anic quotations are to be kept with markers. Let me translate.

**Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He said, "No! So go, both of you, with Our signs; indeed, We are with you, listening."﴾** The plural form in His words ﴿indeed, We are with you, listening﴾ is for magnification (li-al-ta'zim). What Allah, the Majestic and Exalted, mentioned in this verse of His response to Musa, who feared being killed by Fir'awn and his people, was the use of the particle of rebuke (harf al-zajr) which is "kalla" ("No!"). He commanded him to go, he and his brother, with His signs, clarifying for them that Allah is with them. That is, this companionship (ma'iyyah) is a special companionship of support and aid (al-nasr wa al-ta'yid), and that He hears everything they say to them, Fir'awn included. He also clarified this in other places, such as His saying: ﴿He said, "Do not fear; indeed, I am with you both, hearing and seeing."﴾ [Ta-Ha: 46] and His saying: ﴿He said, "We will strengthen your arm through your brother and give you both authority, so they will not reach you. With Our signs, you two and those who follow you will be the victors."﴾ [al-Qasas: 35].

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So come to Pharaoh and say, "Indeed, we are messengers of the Lord of the worlds."﴾

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "Maryam" and "Ta-Ha," and in Surah "Ta-Ha," in discussing His saying, ﴿So say, "Indeed, we are two messengers of your Lord"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 47], we explained the reason for His saying "messengers" in dual form in "Ta-Ha," and its singular form here in "al-Shu'ara'," together with its supporting evidence from the Arabic language.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 26, verse 18:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He said: Did we not bring you up among us as a child?﴾.

The upbringing of Pharaoh for Musa, which he mentioned to him here, is the one whose beginning was mentioned in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the wife of Pharaoh said: "A comfort of the eye for me and for you. Do not kill him; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son," while they did not perceive﴾ [al-Qasas: 9], and in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And I cast upon you love from Me, and that you be raised under My eye﴾ [Ta-Ha: 39].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 26, verse 19:

His saying, may He be exalted, in Pharaoh's speech to Moses: ﴿And you did your deed that you did, and you were of the ungrateful.﴾

Allah, exalted is He, left this deed that he committed unspecified, by expressing it with the indefinite noun, which is the relative pronoun in His saying: "that you did" (allatī fa'alta). He clarified it in other verses and made clear that the deed mentioned is his killing of a man from among them (nafsan minhum):

• As in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So Moses struck him and finished him off﴾ [al-Qasas: 15]

• And His saying: ﴿He said, "My Lord, I have killed a man among them, so I fear that they will kill me"﴾ [al-Qasas: 33], the verse in full.

• And His saying, concerning the Israelite who sought Moses' help twice: ﴿He said, "O Moses, do you intend to kill me as you killed a man yesterday? You intend nothing but to be a tyrant in the land, and you do not intend to be of the reformers."﴾ [al-Qasas: 19].

The most apparent of the opinions to me regarding the meaning of His saying: ﴿And you were of the ungrateful﴾ is that what is intended by it is the ungratefulness for the blessing (kufr al-ni'mah), meaning: We bestowed upon you blessings by raising you as a child, and by our kindness to you, you lived in our blessing, but you were ungrateful for our blessing, and you repaid our kindness with harm by killing a man from among us. As for the other opinions, we have set them aside, because this one is the most apparent to us.

Some people of knowledge said: Moses answered Pharaoh's reminder of the favor of raising him, with His saying: ﴿And this is a favor with which you remind me, that you have enslaved the Children of Israel﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 22]. That is: your enslaving of my people and your humiliating of them does not count as kindness to me, since I am one man of them. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 26, verse 20:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He said, "I did it then, when I was among those astray."﴾ That is: Musa said in reply to Fir'awn, ﴿"I did it then"﴾, i.e., when I did it, I was at that time ﴿"among those astray"﴾, i.e., before God revealed to me and sent me as a messenger. This is the verified meaning of the verse, God willing.

The saying of some scholars, that ﴿"among those astray"﴾ means "among the ignorant," returns to what we have mentioned, because in relation to what God later taught him through revelation, he is considered ignorant before it, i.e., not knowing what God had revealed to him.

We have explained repeatedly in this blessed book that the word ḍalāl (going astray) is used in the Qur'an and in the Arabic language in three senses.

The first sense: ḍalāl is used to mean departing from the reality of a thing. The Arabs say of anyone who has lost knowledge of the reality of something that he "strayed" from it. This straying is a departure from knowledge of something, and it is not straying in religion.

From this meaning is His saying here: ﴿"among those astray"﴾, i.e., among those who have departed from knowledge of the reality of the sciences and secrets that are known only through revelation, because at that time I had not yet been given revelation. From this sense, in its verified usage, is His saying: ﴿"And He found you lost and guided you"﴾ [al-Ḍuḥā: 7], i.e., departing from the sciences He taught you, which cannot be grasped except through revelation.

From this meaning also is His exalted saying: ﴿"He said, 'Its knowledge is with my Lord, in a Book. My Lord neither errs nor forgets.'"﴾ [Ṭā-Hā: 52]. His saying ﴿"My Lord neither errs"﴾ means that the knowledge of nothing, whatever it may be, departs from Him. And His exalted saying: ﴿"If there are not two men, then a man and two women from among those whom you accept as witnesses, so that if one of them errs, the other may remind her."﴾ [al-Baqarah: 282]. His saying ﴿"so that if one of them errs"﴾ means that she departs from knowledge of the reality of what is witnessed, as shown by His following saying: ﴿"the other may remind her"﴾. And His exalted saying about the sons of Ya'qub: ﴿"Indeed our father is in clear error."﴾ [Yūsuf: 8], and His saying: ﴿"They said, 'By God, you are in your old error.'"﴾ [Yūsuf: 95]. All of this is in the verified sense. From this meaning is the saying of the poet:

"Salmā thinks that I seek another in her place,
while I see her wandering in straying (ḍalāl)."

The second sense, which is the well-known one in the language and, in the Qur'an, is the use of ḍalāl for departing from the path of faith to disbelief, from the path of truth to falsehood, and from the path of Paradise to the Fire. From this is His saying: ﴿"not of those who have earned Your anger, nor of those who are astray."﴾ [al-Fātiḥah: 7].

The third sense is the use of ḍalāl for disappearing and dissolving. The Arabs say: "The thing strayed" when it vanished and dissolved. From this is their saying: "The ghee strayed in the food," when it disappeared into it and dissolved. For this reason the Arabs called burial in the grave iḍlāl (causing to stray), because the buried person is consumed by the earth, so he vanishes into it and dissolves.

From this meaning is His exalted saying: ﴿"They say, 'When we have strayed in the earth…'"﴾ [al-Sajdah: 10], meaning: when they are buried and the earth consumes them, so they "stray" in it, i.e., vanish in it and dissolve.

From their use of iḍlāl for burial is the saying of Nābighat Dhubyān, lamenting al-Nu'mān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Abī Shimr al-Ghassānī:

"If you live, I shall not control my own life; and if you die, there is no benefit in life after your death.

So the ones who buried him returned with clear sorrow, and generosity and resolve were left behind in al-Jawlān."

And the saying of al-Mukhabbal al-Sa'dī, lamenting Qays ibn 'Āṣim:

"The sons of Qays ibn Sa'd buried (adallat) their chief,
and the horseman of the age, Qays ibn 'Āṣim."

So the Dhubyānī's saying "fa-āba muḍilluhu" means: his burier returned. The Sa'dī's saying "aḍallat" means: they buried. From the use of ḍalāl for absence and dissolution is also the saying of al-Akhṭal: (p-91)

"You were a speck in a turbid, rough sea,
which the river carried, and it strayed, straying."

And the saying of another:

"Have you not asked, and the abodes would tell you
about the tribe that was lost, where they went?"

Some scholars claimed that ḍalāl has a fourth sense, saying: it is also used for love. He said: from this is His saying: ﴿"By God, you are in your old error"﴾, meaning: in your old love for Yūsuf. He said: from this is the saying of the poet:

"This straying has whitened my forehead and my temples,
and I was not one who had become clear-minded.

How strange of Izzah, in choosing to cut me off,
after the straying, when her cord has worn out."

He also claimed that from this sense is His saying: ﴿"And He found you lost"﴾ [al-Ḍuḥā: 7], meaning: loving guidance, so He guided you. The weakness of this view is not hidden. And God knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 26, verse 21:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So I fled from you when I feared you﴾. His fear of them, which is mentioned here as the cause of his fleeing from them, Allah, exalted is He, has already made clear and explained its cause in His saying: ﴿And there came a man from the farthest part of the city, running. He said, "O Moses, indeed the eminent ones are conspiring against you to kill you, so leave; indeed, I am to you of the sincere advisors." So he left it, fearful and vigilant. He said, "My Lord, save me from the wrongdoing people."﴾ [al-Qasas: 20-21]. And He explained his aforementioned fear by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So he became in the city fearful and vigilant﴾ [al-Qasas: 18], and so on.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then my Lord granted me wisdom and made me among the messengers﴾. We have already presented the verses clarifying the beginning of his prophethood, which is mentioned here, in Surah "Maryam" and elsewhere.

As for His saying: ﴿Then my Lord granted me wisdom﴾, some of them said: "Wisdom (ḥukm) here is prophethood," and among those narrated from on this point is al-Suddi.

The more apparent view to me is that wisdom (ḥukm) is the knowledge which Allah taught him through revelation, and knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 26, verse 23:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Pharaoh said, "And what is the Lord of the worlds?"﴾.

The apparent meaning of this noble verse is that Pharaoh knew nothing about the Lord of the worlds. Likewise is His saying about him: ﴿He said, "Then who is your Lord, O Moses?"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 49], and His saying: ﴿"I know of no god for you other than myself."﴾ [al-Qasas: 38], and His saying: ﴿"If you take a god other than me, I will surely put you among the imprisoned."﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 29]. But Allah, exalted and most high, has made clear that Pharaoh's question in His saying, ﴿And what is the Lord of the worlds?﴾, and His saying, ﴿Then who is your Lord, O Moses?﴾, was the feigned ignorance of one who knows that he is a servant owned by the Lord of the worlds, by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "You know well that none has sent these down but the Lord of the heavens and the earth as evidences; and indeed, I consider you, O Pharaoh, to be one doomed to destruction."﴾ [al-Isra': 102], and His saying, exalted is He, concerning Pharaoh and his people: ﴿And they rejected them, while their souls were convinced of them, out of wrongdoing and arrogance.﴾ [al-Naml: 14].

We have clarified this in surah "Bani Isra'il," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most suitable﴾ [al-Isra': 9], and in surah "Ta-Ha," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "Then who is your Lord, O Moses?"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 49].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 26, verse 30:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said: "Even if I bring you something clear?"﴾ ﴿He said: "Then bring it, if you are of the truthful."﴾ ﴿So he threw his staff,﴾ and so on to the end of the story.

We have already explained this with Qur'anic verses in Surah Ta-Ha and Surah al-A'raf.

The Exalted said: ﴿And recite to them the news of Abraham﴾ ﴿When he said to his father and his people, "What do you worship?"﴾ ﴿They said, "We worship idols, and we remain devoted to them."﴾ — to His saying — ﴿except the Lord of the worlds﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 69–77].

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah Maryam, in our discussion of His saying: ﴿And mention in the Book Abraham﴾ — the verses [Maryam: 41].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 26, verse 94:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then they will be thrown into it, they and the deviators﴾ ﴿And the soldiers of Iblis, all of them﴾. We have already presented the verses that clarify this in several places of this blessed Book: in Surat "Bani Isra'il" (the Children of Israel), in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "Go, and whoever follows you among them, indeed Hell is your recompense, a full recompense"﴾ [al-Isra' 17:63], and in "al-Hijr," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, Hell is the promised place for them all﴾ ﴿It has seven gates; for each gate is a portion designated﴾ [al-Hijr 15:43-44].

(p-93) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They will say, while they are disputing therein﴾ ﴿"By God, we were indeed in clear error, when we made you equal to the Lord of the worlds."﴾

What this noble verse indicates, that the people of the Fire will dispute therein, has been made clear in other places in the Book of God, Exalted is He, such as His saying: ﴿"This is a troop rushing in with you. There is no welcome for them; they will indeed burn in the Fire."﴾ ﴿They will say, "Rather, you — there is no welcome for you! You brought this upon us."﴾ up to His saying: ﴿"Indeed, that is true: the disputing of the people of the Fire."﴾ [Sad: 59–64].

We have already presented the clarification of this with the Qur'anic verses in the surah "al-A'raf," in the discussion of His saying: ﴿"until, when they have all overtaken one another therein, the last of them will say of the first of them, 'Our Lord, these are the ones who led us astray, so give them a double punishment of the Fire.'"﴾ [al-A'raf: 38], and in the surah "al-Baqarah," in the discussion of His saying: ﴿"when those who were followed disown those who followed"﴾, the verse [al-Baqarah: 166].

As for His saying in this noble verse: ﴿"By God, we were indeed in clear error, when we made you equal to the Lord of the worlds."﴾, we have already presented the verses that clarify it at the beginning of the surah "al-An'am," in the discussion of His saying: ﴿"Yet those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord."﴾ [al-An'am: 1].

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then we have no intercessors﴾. We have already mentioned the verses that clarify this in Surat al-Baqarah, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿nor will intercession be accepted from it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 48], and in Surat al-A'raf, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿Do we have any intercessors who might intercede for us?﴾ and the rest of the verse [al-A'raf: 53].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 26, verse 102:

Allah the Exalted said, ﴿So if only we had a return (karrah), so that we might be among the believers﴾. This noble verse indicates two matters. The first of them is that the disbelievers, on the Day of Resurrection, will wish to be returned to the worldly life, because (لَوْ) (law, here expressing wishing, tamanni) in His words here, ﴿So if only we had﴾, is for wishing. The karrah (return) here means the return to the worldly life. They claimed that if they were returned to the worldly life, they would be among the believers who affirm the Messengers in what they brought. We have already mentioned the verses that clarify each of these two matters.

As for their wish to return to the worldly life, we clarified it with Qur'anic verses in Surat al-A'raf, in the discussion of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Or that we be returned so that we may act differently from what we used to do﴾ [al-A'raf: 53]. As for their claim that they would believe if they were returned to the worldly life, we explained the verses that clarify it in al-A'raf, in the discussion of the aforementioned verse, and in al-An'am, in the discussion of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars﴾ [al-An'am: 28].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 26, verse 105:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The people of Noah denied the messengers﴾, and the verses that follow.

We have already presented the discussion of this in Surat al-Hajj and elsewhere, and we discussed His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And I do not ask you for any wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 109, 127, 145, 164, 180] in the story of Noah, Hud, Salih, Lut and Shu'ayb. We have also clarified the verses that explain this in Surat Hud, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And O my people, I do not ask you for any wealth for it; my wage is only from Allah﴾ and the verse [Hud: 29].

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab [Removing the Appearance of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book]):

(p-358) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surat ash-Shu'ara'

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The people of Noah denied the messengers﴾.

This verse indicates that the people of Noah denied a group of messengers, by the evidence of the plural form in His saying "the messengers." Then He clarified that, with what indicates the opposite, namely that they only denied one messenger, who is Noah, upon him and upon our Prophet be prayers and peace, in His saying: ﴿When their brother Noah said to them, "Will you not fear Allah?"﴾ up to His saying: ﴿He said, "My Lord, my people have denied me"﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 106, 117].

The answer to this is that the messengers, upon them be the blessings and peace of Allah, since their call was one and it was "There is no god but Allah," whoever denies one of them is a denier of all of them, as His saying may He be exalted indicates: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no god but I, so worship Me﴾ [al-Anbiya': 25], and His saying: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger﴾ and the verse [an-Nahl: 36]. Allah, may He be exalted, has also made clear that the denier of some of them is a denier of all, in His saying: ﴿And they say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others," and they intend to adopt a way between that. ﴾ ﴿Those are the disbelievers in truth﴾ [an-Nisa': 150-151].

A similar difficulty and its answer come in His saying: ﴿The people of 'Ad denied the messengers﴾ ﴿When their brother Hud said to them﴾ to the end of it [ash-Shu'ara': 123-124], and His saying: ﴿The people of Thamud denied the messengers﴾ ﴿When their brother Salih said to them﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 141-142].

And likewise in the story of Lut and Shu'ayb, upon all of them and upon our Prophet be prayers and peace.

Allah's words: ﴿They said, "Shall we believe you, when the lowest-ranked people follow you?"﴾

We have already discussed this in Surat Hud, in the discussion of His words concerning the people of Nuh: ﴿And we see none following you except those who are the lowest among us﴾ [Hud: 27].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 26, verse 114:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And I am not one to drive away the believers﴾. We have already presented what the Qur'an indicates on this in Surah "Hud," in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted, concerning Noah: ﴿And I am not one to drive away those who have believed. Indeed, they are to meet their Lord, but I see you as a people who are ignorant﴾ ﴿And O my people, who would protect me from Allah if I drove them away?﴾ [Hud: 29-30].

We also clarified it with Qur'anic verses in Surah "al-An'am," in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, seeking His face,﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And so you would drive them away and thereby be among the wrongdoers﴾ [al-An'am: 52]. And in Surah "al-Kahf," in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And keep yourself patient with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, seeking His face﴾ [al-Kahf: 28].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 26, verse 117:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed my people have denied me."﴾ ﴿So judge decisively between me and them, and save me and those with me of the believers.﴾ ﴿So We saved him and those with him in the laden ship.﴾ ﴿Then We drowned the rest afterward.﴾ His saying, may He be exalted, here about Noah: ﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed my people have denied me,"﴾ He clarified it in other than this place;

• like His saying: ﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed I have invited my people night and day. But my invitation has only increased them in flight. And indeed, every time I invited them that You may forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears, covered themselves with their garments, persisted, and became arrogant with [great] arrogance."﴾ [Noah: 5–7]. And His saying here: ﴿So judge decisively between me and them﴾, meaning: decide between me and them with a decision. This decision which he asked his Lord for is the destruction of the disbelievers, and the saving of him and those who believed with him, as He, exalted, clarified in other verses;

• like His saying, exalted: ﴿So he called upon his Lord, "Indeed, I am overpowered, so avenge [me]."﴾ [al-Qamar: 10]

• and His saying, exalted: ﴿And Noah said, "My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant."﴾ [Noah: 26], and other verses. And His saying here about Noah: ﴿and save me and those with me of the believers﴾, He has explained in many verses that He answered this supplication of his;

• like His saying here: ﴿So We saved him and those with him in the laden ship,﴾

• and His saying, exalted: ﴿So We saved him and the companions of the ship﴾ – the verse [al-'Ankabut: 15]

• and His saying, exalted: ﴿And Noah had certainly called Us, and We are the best of responders. And We saved him and his family from the great distress.﴾ [al-Saffat: 75–76]

The verses of this kind are many.

And His saying here: ﴿Then We drowned the rest afterward,﴾ has come explained in many verses; like His saying, exalted: ﴿So the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 14], and His saying, exalted: ﴿And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed, they are to be drowned.﴾ [Hud: 37], and other verses.

Al-mashhun (المَشْحُون) means the filled. From it is the saying of 'Ubayd ibn al-Abras:

"We filled their land with horses until we left them more humbled than the path."

Al-fulk (الفُلْك) is applied to the singular and the plural. If it is applied to the singular, its masculine form is permissible, like His saying here: ﴿in the laden ship (al-fulk al-mashhun)﴾; and if it is used as a plural, it is feminine. What is meant by al-fulk here is the ship (al-safinah), as Allah, exalted, explicitly stated in His saying: ﴿So We saved him and the companions of the ship﴾ – the verse [al-'Ankabut: 15].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 26, verse 176:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The companions of the Thicket denied the messengers﴾. Most of the scholars said: The companions of the Thicket (al-Aykah) are the people of Madyan. Ibn Kathir said: "This is the correct view, and accordingly this verse is explained by the clear verses that relate the story of Shu'ayb with Madyan." Among the evidence used by the proponents of this view is that he said here to the companions of the Thicket: ﴿Give full measure and do not be among the cheaters. And weigh with an even balance. And do not deprive people of their due and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 181-183]. And this speech, which Allah mentioned from him, was said to Madyan on several occasions, as in His saying in "Hud": ﴿And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. And do not diminish from the measure and the scale. Indeed, I see you in prosperity, and indeed, I fear for you the punishment of an all-encompassing day."﴾ ﴿And O my people, give full measure and weight with justice and do not deprive people of their due and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption. What remains [for you] from Allah is better for you, if you should be believers﴾ [Hud: 84-86], and other verses besides these.

We have already stated in surah "al-A'raf" our view: If it is said that the destruction that befell the people of Shu'ayb, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned in "al-A'raf" that it was an earthquake (rajfah), and mentioned in "Hud" that it was a blast (sayhah), and mentioned in "al-Shu'ara" that it was the punishment of the Day of the Canopy (yawm al-zullah).

The answer is what Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his tafsir. He said: "All of that came upon them together: the punishment of the Day of the Canopy befell them, which was a cloud that shaded them, in which were sparks of fire, flame and great heat; then a blast came upon them from the sky, and a violent earthquake from the earth beneath them, so the souls departed, the spirits flowed out, and the bodies became still." End of quote. And according to the view that Shu'ayb was sent to two communities, Madyan and the companions of the Thicket, and that Madyan were not the companions of the Thicket, there is no difficulty. This has come in a weak hadith from Abdullah ibn Amr, and among those who transmitted this view from him are Qatadah, Ikrimah and Ishaq ibn Bishr.

We have already presented some of the verses that clarify this in surah "al-Hijr", in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And indeed, the companions of the Thicket were wrongdoers﴾ ﴿So We took vengeance upon them﴾ [al-Hijr: 78-79]. There we also explained that Nafi', Ibn Amir and Ibn Kathir read "Layka" in surah "al-Shu'ara" and surah "Sad" with a fathah on the lam at the beginning of the word and a fathah on the ta' at its end, without a hamza and without the definite article, on the basis that the name of the town is diptote (ghayr munsarif); and that the rest read "al-Aykah" with the definite article, a hamza, and a kasrah on the ta'; and that all of them agreed on this in "Qaf" and "al-Hijr". We also explained there the justification (tawjih) of the two readings in "al-Shu'ara" and "Sad", and the meaning of "al-Aykah" linguistically, along with some Arabic supporting examples.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 26, verse 184:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And fear Him who created you and the earlier generations﴾. Al-jibillah (the created kind, creation): it means the creation. From it is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And he had already led astray a great multitude of you﴾ [Ya-Sin: 62], where the word jibillan means a multitude. Ibn Zayd used the verse in Surat Ya-Sin mentioned here as evidence for this verse of ash-Shu'ara', and Ibn Kathir transmitted this from him. From this is the saying of the poet:

"Death is the greatest of events that pass over the jibillah."

(p-٩٧) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And indeed, it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾ ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down﴾ ﴿upon your heart, that you may be among the warners﴾ ﴿in a clear Arabic tongue﴾.

In this noble verse, may He be glorified and exalted, Allah affirms that this Mighty Qur'an is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds, that the Trustworthy Spirit, who is Jibril, brought it down upon the heart of our Prophet, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them both, so that he might be among those who warn by it, and that it was revealed to him in a clear Arabic tongue. What He mentions here He has clarified in other places.

As for this Qur'an being a revelation from the Lord of the worlds, Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, has clarified this in several verses of His Book, such as:

• His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, it is a noble Qur'an, in a Book well-guarded, which none touches except the purified, a revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 77-79].

• His saying: ﴿And it is not the word of a poet; little do you believe. Nor is it the word of a soothsayer; little do you reflect. It is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Haqqah: 41-43].

• His saying: ﴿Ta-Ha. We did not send down the Qur'an to you to be distressed, but as a reminder for one who fears, a revelation from He who created the earth and the high heavens﴾ [Ta-Ha: 1-4].

• His saying: ﴿The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 2].

• His saying: ﴿Ha-Mim. A revelation from the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful, a Book whose verses have been detailed, an Arabic Qur'an﴾, to the end of the verse [Fussilat: 1-3].

• His saying: ﴿Ya-Sin. By the wise Qur'an, indeed you are among the messengers, upon a straight path, a revelation of the Mighty, the Merciful, that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, so they are heedless﴾ [Ya-Sin: 1-6].

And verses similar to these are many.

His saying: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down﴾, He also explained this in other places, such as His saying: ﴿Say, whoever is an enemy to Jibril, then indeed he has brought it down upon your heart by the permission of Allah﴾, to the end of the verse [al-Baqarah: 97].

His saying: ﴿that you may be among the warners﴾ means: it was revealed to you for the purpose that you may be among those who warn by it. This is explained in other verses, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim, Sad. A Book revealed to you, so let there be no constriction in your breast about it, that you may warn by it﴾, to the end of the verse [al-A'raf: 1-2], meaning: it was revealed to you so that you may warn by it.

And His saying: ﴿a revelation of the Mighty, the Merciful, that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned﴾, to the end of the verse [Ya-Sin: 5-6].

His saying: ﴿in a clear Arabic tongue﴾, He also mentioned this in other places, such as His saying: ﴿The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue﴾ [al-Nahl: 103], and His saying: ﴿A Book whose verses have been detailed, an Arabic Qur'an﴾, to the end of the verse [Fussilat: 3].

We have already explained the meaning of the "Arabic tongue" with its evidences in Surah "al-Nahl," in the discussion of His saying: ﴿And this is a clear Arabic tongue﴾ [al-Nahl: 103]. And we have clarified the meaning of Jibril's bringing down the Qur'an (p-٩٨) upon his heart ﷺ with the Qur'anic verses in Surah "al-Baqarah," in the discussion of His saying: ﴿Say, whoever is an enemy to Jibril, then indeed he has brought it down upon your heart by the permission of Allah﴾, to the end of the verse [al-Baqarah: 97].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 26, verse 198:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And had We sent it down upon some of the non-Arabs﴾ ﴿and he had recited it to them, they would not have been believers in it.﴾ We have already presented this noble verse, along with the verses that clarify it in "al-Nahl" (The Bee), in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The tongue of the one they refer to is non-Arab﴾ [al-Nahl: 103] and so on.

Know that every sound that is not Arabic, the Arabs call a'jam (non-Arabic, foreign), even if it comes from a non-rational creature. From this is the saying of Humayd ibn Thawr, describing the sound of a dove:

"I have not seen one like me moved by the call of its kind, nor an Arab moved by the call of a non-Arabic (a'jam) sound."

The statement of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Thus We have caused it to enter into the hearts of the criminals.﴾ ﴿They will not believe in it until they see the painful punishment.﴾

His saying "salaknahu" (we caused it to enter) means "adkhalnahu" (we caused it to enter). As we have already explained, with Qur'anic verses and Arabic evidence, in the commentary on Surah Hud, in discussing the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿We said: Load therein two of each kind, two.﴾ [Hud: 40]. The pronoun in "salaknahu" is said to refer to the Qur'an, and this is the more apparent view. It is also said to refer to the denial and disbelief mentioned in His saying: ﴿They were not believers in it.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 199]. These disbelievers, whom Allah, Majestic and Exalted, mentions in this noble verse as those who will not believe until they see the painful punishment, are those upon whom the word of punishment has been justified, and it had already preceded in Allah's knowledge that they are wretched. This is shown by His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been justified will not believe, even if every sign should come to them, until they see the painful punishment.﴾ [Yunus: 96-97]. We have clarified the severity of these people's obstinacy, and that they do not believe in the signs, in Surah al-Furqan and Surah Bani Isra'il and elsewhere.

His saying, ﴿Thus We have caused it to enter﴾, is a qualifier (na't) of an omitted verbal noun (masdar, the noun of the action), meaning: "Thus is the threading (al-salk), that is, the causing to enter; We caused it to enter into the hearts of the criminals." Its clarification, if the pronoun refers to the Qur'an, is that Allah sent it down upon an eloquent Arab man, in clear Arabic tongue. They heard it and understood it, because it was in their language, and its meanings entered their hearts; but they did not believe in it, because the word of punishment was justified against them. And if the pronoun in "salaknahu" refers to disbelief and denial, then His saying about them, ﴿They were not believers in it﴾, indicates the entry of disbelief and denial into their hearts. That is: "Thus is the threading, We threaded it," and so on.

(p-99) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then they will say, "Will we be reprieved?"﴾.

The word "هل" (hal) here is used to express wishing (tamanni), and the verse indicates that they wished for delay and respite, i.e., postponement. Other verses clearly show that they asked for this, and that they were not granted what they requested, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And warn mankind of the Day when the punishment will come to them, and those who did wrong will say, "Our Lord, delay us for a near term; we will answer Your call and follow the messengers." Had you not sworn before that there would be no decline for you?﴾ [Ibrahim: 44]. And He made clear that they will not be given respite in some of His verses, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So they will not be able to avert it, nor will they be reprieved﴾ [al-Anbiya: 40], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Nor were they then given respite﴾ [al-Dukhan: 29], along with other verses.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 26, verse 204:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then is it of Our punishment that they seek to hasten?﴾ We have already presented the verses clarifying this in Surah "al-Ra'd" (Thunder), in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they ask you to hasten the evil before the good﴾ [al-Ra'd: 6], and we mentioned a portion of it in Surah "Yunus," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if His punishment should come upon you by night or by day, what part of it would the criminals seek to hasten?﴾ ﴿Then, when it has occurred, will you believe in it? Now? And you had been [previously] seeking to hasten it!﴾ [Yunus: 50-51].

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Have you considered, if We let them enjoy for years,﴾ ﴿and then there comes to them what they were promised,﴾ ﴿what they were given of enjoyment will not avail them.﴾

We have already explained this in Surat "al-Baqarah," in the discussion of His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Each one of them wishes he could be given a life of a thousand years, but that would not remove him from the punishment that he be granted life.﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 96]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We never destroyed a town but that it had warners⁠﻿﻿ (mundhirun) for it﴾. We have already presented its clarification with Qur'anic verses in Surat Bani Isra'il (the Chapter of the Children of Israel), in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We would never punish until We send a messenger﴾ [al-Isra': 15].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 26, verse 209:

His saying, Most High: ﴿A reminder, and We were not unjust.﴾ We have already presented the verses that indicate this, such as His saying, Most High: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong the people anything, but it is the people who wrong themselves﴾ [Yunus: 44], and His saying, Most High: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong even the weight of an atom; and if it is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward﴾ [An-Nisa': 40] (p-100), and other verses besides these. As for His saying, dhikra (a reminder), some of them (the grammarians) parsed it in the nominative, on the basis that it is the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: this is a reminder. And some of them parsed it in the accusative, and in its parsing as an accusative there are several possibilities. Among them: that it is a substitute for the absolute object (al-maf'ul al-mutlaq, the cognate accusative) from His saying "mundhirun" (warners), because andhara (to warn) and dhakara (to remind) are close in meaning.

And among them: that it is an object of purpose (maf'ul min ajlihi, the accusative of cause or purpose), meaning: they warn for the sake of the reminder, in the sense of admonition (tadhkira).

And among them: that it is a circumstantial clause (hal, the accusative of state) from the pronoun in "mundhirun," meaning: they warn them while being people of reminder (dhawi tadhkira).

Allah's statement: ﴿Indeed, they are removed from hearing [the heavenly message]﴾. We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "al-Hijr," in the discussion of His statement: ﴿And We have placed in the sky great stars and made them attractive to observers. And We have protected them﴾ [al-Hijr: 16-17].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 26, verse 213:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So do not invoke with Allah another deity, lest you be among those punished﴾. We have already explained in the surah of "Banu Isra'il" (Surat al-Isra'), in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do not makes another god with Allah, lest you sit reproached and forsaken﴾ [al-Isra' 22], by the Qur'anic evidence, that the Prophet (ﷺ) is addressed with this kind of address, and that the intended meaning is legislation for his ummah (community), together with some Arabic evidences. His saying here, ﴿So do not invoke with Allah another deity﴾, and so on, has the same meaning in many verses:

• Such as His saying: ﴿Do not make another god with Allah, lest you sit reproached and forsaken﴾ [al-Isra' 22].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not make another god with Allah, lest you be thrown into Hell, blamed and banished﴾ [al-Isra' 39].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If you associate others with Him, your deeds will surely be nullified﴾ [al-Zumar 65].

And other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 26, verse 214:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾. This command in this noble verse, to warn specifically his closest kinsmen, does not contradict the command to give general warning, as the Qur'anic verses indicate by such as:

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion (al-Furqan) upon His servant that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾ [al-Furqan: 1]

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿This Qur'an has been revealed to me that I may warn you thereby and whoever it reaches﴾ [al-An'am: 19]

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you warn thereby a people contentious﴾ [Maryam: 97]

And the verses of this kind are many.

(p-101) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And lower your wing to those of the believers who follow you﴾. We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surat al-Ma'idah, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him, humble toward the believers, mighty against the disbelievers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 54]. And in Surat al-Hijr, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And lower your wing to the believers﴾ [al-Hijr: 88]. We promised in Surat Bani Isra'il, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him, and to parents, good treatment﴾ [al-Isra': 23], that we would clarify the meaning of lowering the wing and its attribution to humility, in Surat al-Shu'ara', at this place. This is our fulfillment of that promise. For its fulfillment it suffices us to transmit our discussion from our treatise entitled: "Man' Jawaz al-Majaz fi al-Munazzal li-l-Ta'abbud wa al-I'jaz" (The Prohibition of the Permissibility of Majaz (figurative usage) in the Revealed Text for Worship and Inimitability).

In it we said, and its text is: The answer to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And lower to them the wing of humility﴾ [al-Isra': 24] is that the "wing" here is used in its literal sense (haqiqah), because the word "janah" (wing) in the language is applied literally to a person's hand, upper arm, and armpit. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And draw in your arm (janahak) against terror﴾ [al-Qasas: 32]. And "lowering" is used in its real meaning, which is the opposite of raising, because one who intends to strike raises his wings, while the display of humility and submission lowers his wings. So the command to lower the wing to the two parents is a kinayah (allusion or metonymy) for gentleness of demeanor toward them and humility toward them, just as He said to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿And lower your wing to those who follow you of the believers﴾. The Arabs' use of "lowering the wing" as a kinayah for humility and gentleness of demeanor is a well-known style, and from it is the saying of the poet:

You are famed for lowering the wing,
so do not be, in raising it, a falcon.

As for the attribution of the wing to humility (dhull), it does not necessitate majaz, as many suppose, because the idafah (construct phrase) in it is like the idafah in your saying: "Hatim of generosity" (Hatim al-Jud).

So the meaning is: "And lower to them the wing that is humbled by mercy," or "the docile (dhalul) wing" according to the reading of dhull with a kasrah (dhill). As for what is reported from Abu Tammam, that when he said:

Do not give me to drink the water of blame, for I am a lover
who has found the water of my weeping sweet,

a man came to him and said: "Pour for me in this vessel some of the water of blame." He said to him: "If you bring me a feather from the wing of humility, I will pour for you some of the water of blame." (p-102) There is no proof in this, because the verse does not intend that humility has a wing. What is intended is the lowering of a wing characterized by humility toward the two parents out of mercy toward them. At most, this is the idafah of the qualified noun to its attribute, like "Hatim of generosity." Its parallel in the Qur'an is the idafah in His saying: ﴿the rain of evil﴾ [al-Furqan: 40], and ﴿the punishment of humiliation﴾ [al-An'am: 93], meaning: the rain of stones of sijjil, qualified by its evil for whomever it falls upon, and the punishment of the people of the Fire, qualified by its humiliation for whomever it falls upon. What justifies the idafah of the specific "wing" to humility, even though humility is an attribute of the person and not of the wing itself, is that lowering the wing is used as a kinayah for a person's humility, submission, and gentleness of demeanor toward his parents out of mercy for them. And the attribution of attributes of the essence to some of its parts is one of the styles of the Arabic language, like the attribution of lying and error to the forelock in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿a lying, sinning forelock﴾ [al-'Alaq: 16], and like the attribution of humility, toil, and exhaustion to faces in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Faces that day will be humbled, laboring and exhausted﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 2–3]. Similar examples are numerous in the Qur'an and in the speech of the Arabs. This is the apparent meaning of the verse, and the speech of the early exegetes (salaf) indicates it.

Ibn al-Qayyim said in "al-Sawa'iq": The meaning of the idafah of the wing to humility is that humility has a metaphorical wing (janah ma'nawi) suited to it, not a wing of feathers. And Allah knows best. The end of the quotation. In it is clarification of the meaning of lowering the wing.

The verification is that the idafah of the wing to humility is an idafah of the qualified to its attribute, as we have explained, and knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He. Al-Zamakhshari said in "al-Kashshaf," in his commentary on His saying: ﴿of the believers who follow you﴾: If you say: those who follow the Messenger are the believers, and the believers are those who follow the Messenger, then what is His saying: ﴿of the believers who follow you﴾?

I say: In it there are two aspects. One: that He calls them believers before they enter into faith, because they are approaching it. Two: that by "the believers" is meant those who affirm with their tongues, and they are of two kinds: a kind who affirmed and followed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in what he brought, and a kind of whom nothing was found except affirmation alone, and then they are either hypocrites or wicked. The hypocrite and the wicked person are not to be given the lowering of the wing.

The meaning is: the believers among your kinsfolk and others. That is: warn your people, so if they follow you and obey you, then lower your wing to them; and if they disobey you and do not follow you, then disassociate yourself from them and from their deeds of polytheism with Allah and other than Him. The end of what is from him.

(p-103) And what appears to me most correct regarding His saying: ﴿of the believers who follow you﴾ is that it is a kind of emphasis (tawkid) of which the like is frequent in the Mighty Qur'an:

• Like His saying: ﴿They say with their mouths﴾ [Al 'Imran: 167], and it is known that they only say with their mouths.

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So woe to those who write the Scripture with their own hands﴾ [al-Baqarah: 79], and it is known that they only write it with their hands.

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Nor a bird that flies with its two wings﴾ [al-An'am: 38].

• And His saying: ﴿out of envy from themselves﴾ [al-Baqarah: 109].

And so on, among other verses.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 26, verse 217:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And put your trust in the Mighty, the Merciful﴾ ﴿Who sees you when you stand up﴾ ﴿and your movements among those who prostrate﴾.

We have already mentioned, in the introduction to this blessed book, that among the types of clarification (bayan) it contains is that some scholars state an opinion regarding a verse while there is a contextual indicator (qarinah) within the verse showing that this opinion is not sound. We gave several examples of this in the introduction and in what has passed of the book.

Knowing this, be aware that His saying here, ﴿and your movements among those who prostrate﴾, some people of knowledge (ahl al-'ilm) have said its meaning is: "and your movements in the loins of your prostrating fathers," i.e., the believers in God, such as Adam, Noah, Abraham and Ishmael.

Some have used as evidence for this view regarding the forefathers after Abraham His saying, may He be exalted, about Abraham: ﴿And He made it a lasting word among his descendants﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 28]. Among those reported to have held this view is Ibn 'Abbas, as al-Qurtubi transmitted it from him. But there is a contextual indicator within the verse showing that this view is not sound, namely His saying, may He be exalted, before it and linked to it: ﴿Who sees you when you stand up﴾. For He did not intend by it that he would stand in the loins of the fathers, by consensus. The beginning of the verse is linked to its end, i.e., "Who sees you when you stand up" to your prayer, and when you rise from your bed and your place of sitting, and [He sees] ﴿your movements among those who prostrate﴾, i.e., those who pray, according to the most apparent of the opinions, because he (ﷺ) would move among those praying, standing, prostrating and bowing. Some have said: ﴿Who sees you when you stand up﴾, i.e., to prayer, alone, and ﴿your movements among those who prostrate﴾, i.e., those who pray when you lead the people in prayer.

His saying here, ﴿Who sees you when you stand up﴾ and what follows, indicates the care (i'tina') given to him (ﷺ), and His saying, may He be exalted, clarifies this: ﴿And be patient for the judgment of your Lord, for indeed you are within Our eyes﴾ [at-Tur: 48].

As for His saying, ﴿And put your trust﴾, it was read by the majority of the seven readers except Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir with the waw (wa-tawakkal). Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read it with the fa' (fa-tawakkal). Some copies of the 'Uthmanic Mushaf contain the waw and some contain the fa'. As for His saying here, ﴿And put your trust in the Mighty, the Merciful﴾, we have already presented the verses clarifying it in Surah al-Fatihah, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatihah: 5]. We have expanded on its clarification with Qur'anic verses, together with an explanation of the meaning of tawakkul (trust in God), in Surah Bani Isra'il, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We gave Moses the Book and made it a guidance for the Children of Israel: "Take not other than Me as Disposer of affairs (wakil)"﴾ [al-Isra': 2].

The Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 26, verse 224:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them.﴾ "Ash-shu'ara'" (the poets) is the plural of "shā'ir" (poet), like "jāhil" (ignorant) and "juhalā'" (ignorant ones), and "ʿālim" (scholar) and "ʿulamā'" (scholars). "Yattabiʿuhumu al-ghāwūn" (those who go astray follow them): "al-ghāwūn" is the plural of "ghāwin," who is the one who is astray. His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse, ﴿those who go astray follow them﴾, indicates that following the poets is part of following Satan, as evidenced by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, My servants—you have no authority over them, except those of the deviators who follow you﴾ [al-Hijr: 42]. Nafi' alone recited this letter as "yattabiʿuhumu" with a sukun on the taʾ (the two-dotted letter, taʾ muthannāh) and a fatha on the bāʾ (the one-dotted letter, bāʾ muwahhadah). The rest recited it as "yattabiʿuhumu" with a shaddah on the taʾ and a kasra on the bāʾ, and both readings have the same meaning.

What He, exalted is He, mentioned in this noble verse, in His saying ﴿And the poets—those who go astray follow them﴾, indicates the refutation of the disbelievers in their claim that the Prophet ﷺ is a poet, because those whom those who go astray follow cannot be among them, and the Prophet ﷺ cannot be one of them.

What clarifies this meaning are the verses that came explaining that they claimed against him ﷺ that he is a poet, and God's refutation of them in that. As for their claim that he ﷺ is a poet, He, exalted is He, mentioned it in His saying about them: ﴿Rather, they said, "A confusion of dreams." Rather, he has invented it. Rather, he is a poet﴾ [al-Anbiya': 5], and the verse.

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they say, "Shall we really abandon our gods for a mad poet?"﴾ [al-Saffat: 36]

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Or do they say, "A poet, for whom we await the misfortunes of time"?﴾ [al-Tur: 30]

As for God's refutation of them in that, He mentioned it in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it is not the word of a poet—little do you believe﴾, the verse [al-Haqqah: 41].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it befitting for him. It is only a reminder and a clear Qur'an﴾ [Ya-Sin: 69]

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they say, "Shall we really abandon our gods for a mad poet?" Rather, he has come with the truth and confirmed the messengers﴾ [al-Saffat: 36–37];

because His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Rather, he has come with the truth﴾, the verse, is a refutation of them in their saying that he is a mad poet.

* *

Two issues are connected to this noble verse.

The first issue: Know that it is established from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "That the belly of a man be filled with pus that consumes it is better for him than that it be filled with poetry," narrated by the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) in their Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him. His saying in the hadith: "yarīhi" with a fatha on the upper two-dotted letter (yāʾ muthannāh taḥtiyyah) and a kasra on the rāʾ after it, followed by a yāʾ, is the present tense of "wara al-qayḥu jawfahu, yarīhi, warīyan," meaning when pus consumes and corrupts it. The most apparent view is that the origin of "warāhu" is that it struck his lung with corruption.

Know also that the verification that should not be deviated from is that poetry is speech: its good is good, and its ugly is ugly.

Among the Qur'anic proofs for that: when He, exalted is He, censured the poets, with His saying ﴿those who go astray follow them﴾ ﴿Do you not see that they wander in every valley﴾ ﴿and that they say what they do not do﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 224–226], He made an exception of those who believed and did righteous deeds, in His saying: ﴿except those who believed, did righteous deeds, and remembered Allah much﴾, the verse [al-Shu'ara': 227].

By what we have mentioned, you know that the verification is that the authentic hadith explicitly stating that filling the belly with pus, which corrupts it, is better than filling it with poetry, is to be understood as applying to one who devoted himself to poetry and was occupied with it instead of remembrance, recitation of the Qur'an, and obedience to Allah, exalted is He, and to ugly poetry that includes falsehood and vanity, such as mentioning wine and the beauty of non-related women, and the like.

* *

The second issue: Know that the scholars differed concerning a poet who confesses in his poetry to what requires a prescribed punishment (hadd): is the hadd to be enforced upon him? There are two opinions. One of them: it is enforced upon him, because he acknowledged it, and acknowledgment establishes prescribed punishments.

The second: he is not punished on the basis of his confession in poetry, because a poet's lying in his poetry is a well-known, customary matter, occurring without dispute.

Its author (al-Shinqiti), may Allah pardon him and forgive him, said: The more apparent of the two opinions to me is that when a poet confesses in his poetry to what requires the hadd, the hadd is not enforced upon him, because Allah, majestic and exalted, explicitly stated here their lying in their poetry in His saying: ﴿and that they say what they do not do﴾, so this noble verse averts the hadd from them. (p-106) However, the more apparent view is that if he acknowledges that, his acknowledgment makes him deserving of blame and disciplinary correction, even though he is not subject to the hadd on its account, as a group of the people of reports mentioned in the famous story of Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, with al-Nu'man ibn 'Adi ibn Nadlah.

Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his commentary on this noble verse: It has been mentioned from Muhammad ibn Ishaq and Muhammad ibn Sa'd in "al-Tabaqat," and al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar in the book "al-Fukahah," that Amir al-Mu'minin Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, appointed al-Nu'man ibn 'Adi ibn Nadlah over Maysan, from the land of Basra, and he used to recite poetry. He said:

Have you not heard that the beautiful woman's husband
In Maysan is given to drink in glass and in a jar?

When I wish, the landowners of a village sing to me,
And a dancing girl who steps on every ankle-bracelet.

So if you are my boon companion, then pour me the largest,
And do not pour me the smallest, the chipped one.

Perhaps the Commander of the Faithful would be displeased
By our drinking together in the ruined palace.

When that reached Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, he said: "Indeed, by Allah, that does displease me. Whoever meets him, let him inform him that I have dismissed him," and Umar wrote to him: "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. ﴿Ha-Mim﴾ ﴿The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Knowing﴾ ﴿Forgiver of sin and Acceptor of repentance, Severe in punishment, Possessor of bounty. There is no deity except Him; to Him is the final return﴾ [Ghafir: 1–3]. To proceed: your saying has reached me:

Perhaps the Commander of the Faithful would be displeased
By our drinking together in the ruined palace.

By Allah, it does displease me, and I have dismissed you." When he came to Umar, Umar rebuked him with this poetry. He said: "By Allah, O Commander of the Faithful, I have never drunk it at all, and that poetry was only something that welled up on my tongue." Umar said: "I think so, but by Allah, you will never work for me as an official again, since you have said what you have said." He was not reported to have been given the hadd for drinking, though he had included it in his poetry, because "they say what they do not do," but Umar censured him, blamed him for that, and dismissed him on account of it. End of the relevant part of Ibn Kathir's words. This story is cited as supporting what we have mentioned.

Also, more than one historian mentioned that Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Malik, when he heard the saying of al-Farazdaq:

So they spent the night beside me, thrown down,
And I spent the night undoing the seals of the sealed vessels.

said to him: "The hadd has become obligatory upon you." Al-Farazdaq said: "O Commander of the Faithful, Allah has averted the hadd from me (p-107) by His saying: ﴿and that they say what they do not do﴾," so he did not punish him despite his acknowledgment of what requires the hadd.

The Almighty's statement: ﴿And that they say what they do not do﴾. What is mentioned here about "the poets," that they say what they do not do, He explained in another verse that it is among the causes of hatred (maqt) in His sight, may He be exalted. This is in His statement: ﴿O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?﴾ ﴿Greatly hateful in the sight of Allah is that you say what you do not do﴾ [al-Saff: 2-3]. And maqt in the language of the Arabs is intense hatred (al-bughd al-shadid). So a person's saying what he does not do, as mentioned regarding poetry, is something Allah hates, although saying what one does not do varies in degree (tafawut), and Allah knows best.

(p. 108)

**Allah's words: "Except those who believe and do righteous deeds."** ﴿إلّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ﴾ We have already set out the verses that clarify this in the beginning of Surah "al-Kahf," in the discussion of Allah's words: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds, that for them is a good reward﴾ [al-Kahf: 2], together with their Arabic evidences.

* *

**Allah's words: "And they remember Allah much."** ﴿وَذَكَرُوا اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا﴾ In this noble verse, Allah praises those who believe and do righteous deeds for their remembering Allah much. The remembrance of Allah for which He praised them here is the very thing He commanded in other verses, and He explained its reward. Allah says: ﴿And remember Allah much, that you may prosper﴾ [al-Anfal: 45]. He also says: ﴿O you who believe, remember Allah with much remembrance, and glorify Him morning and evening﴾ [al-Ahzab: 41–42]. And He says: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, are signs for people of understanding, who remember Allah standing, sitting, and on their sides﴾ [Al 'Imran: 190–191], and so on. He also says: ﴿And the men who remember Allah much and the women who remember, Allah has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward﴾ [al-Ahzab: 35].

* *

**Allah's words: "And they defend themselves after they have been wronged."** ﴿وانْتَصَرُوا مِن بَعْدِ ما ظُلِمُوا﴾ We have already set out the verses that clarify this, such as His words: ﴿And whoever defends himself after being wronged, those—there is no blame upon them. The blame is only upon those who wrong people﴾ [al-Shura: 41–42], at the end of Surah "al-Nahl," in the discussion of His words: ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were afflicted. But if you are patient, it is better for the patient﴾ [al-Nahl: 126].

* *

**Allah's words: "And those who wronged will know what return they will be returned to."** ﴿وَسَيَعْلَمُ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا أيَّ مُنْقَلَبٍ يَنْقَلِبُونَ﴾ *Al-munqalab* here means the return and the destination. The more apparent view is that here it is a *mimi* verbal noun (masdar mimi, a noun of place or action formed with a prefixed mim). It is established in the science of *sarf* (morphology) that when a verb exceeds three letters, each of its *mimi* verbal noun, its noun of place (*ism al-makan*), and its noun of time (*ism al-zaman*) takes the form of the passive participle (*ism al-maf'ul*).

The meaning is: "And those who wronged will know what return they will return to, and what destination they will arrive at." What this noble verse indicates, namely that the wrongdoers will know on the Day of Resurrection the return to which they are returning, that is, they will know the evil consequence which is their outcome, their destination, and their return, has come in many verses, such as:

• His words: ﴿No! You are going to know. Then, no! You are going to know. No! If you knew with the certainty of knowledge, you would surely see the Hellfire. Then you will surely see it with the certainty of sight﴾ [al-Takathur: 3–7].

• His words: ﴿And they will know, when they see the punishment, who is more astray in way﴾ [al-Furqan: 42].

• His words: ﴿And the disbelievers will know to whom belongs the ultimate home﴾ [al-Ra'd: 42].

The verses of this kind are very numerous.

As for His words *"ayya munqalab"* (what return): it takes the place of the absolute object (*al-mutlaq*) from His words *"yanqalibun"* (they will return). It is not an object (*maf'ul bihi*) of His words *"sa-ya'lamu"* (will know). Al-Qurtubi said: "*Ayya* is in the accusative as an object of *yanqalibun*, and it has the meaning of a verbal noun. It is not permissible for it to be in the accusative governed by *sa-ya'lamu*, because *ayya* and the rest of the interrogative particles are not governed by what precedes them, according to what the grammarians have mentioned." Al-Nahhas said: "The reality of this matter is that the interrogative has a meaning of its own, and what precedes it has another meaning. So if what precedes it governed it, some meanings would enter into others." End of his quotation. And Allah knows best.
